wages.text: He supports union organizing, collective bargaining, prevailing-wage standards, and stronger enforcement of labor law.
wages.quote: Protect the right of workers to organize and bargain collectively

debt.text: He opposes Social Security benefit cuts and raising the retirement age, and supports protecting Medicare from cuts and privatization.
debt.quote: Erik will oppose cuts to Social Security benefits and efforts to raise the retirement age.

housing.text: He supports increasing housing supply and removing unnecessary barriers that slow development.
housing.quote: Erik supports practical steps to increase housing supply, including incentives for affordable housing construction, infrastructure investments that make new housing possible, and removing unnecessary barriers that slow responsible development.

schools.text: He supports strengthening public schools and restoring federal education funding, including Title I.
schools.quote: Erik supports restoring and expanding federal education support, including Title I, so quality education does not depend on a student’s ZIP code.

guns.text: He supports background checks, waiting periods, and red-flag laws with due-process protections while defending lawful gun ownership.
guns.quote: Support background checks that keep guns out of the hands of people who should not have them

abortion.text: He supports restoring federal protections for reproductive rights and opposes abortion bans without exceptions for rape, incest, or the mother’s health.
abortion.quote: The decision to continue or end a pregnancy is one of the most personal decisions a person can face.

health.text: He supports protecting Medicare and Medicaid, restoring ACA subsidies, and expanding access to affordable coverage, including through public options.
health.quote: He is open to serious conversations about the best way to get there, including single-payer models, Medicare for All, public options, and other approaches that expand access and lower costs.

energy.text: He says climate change should be taken seriously and supports investing in clean energy such as wind and solar.
energy.quote: That means taking climate change seriously, investing in clean energy, keeping public lands public, protecting the Boundary Waters, and supporting farmers as partners in long-term stewardship.

voting.text: He opposes voter-suppression tactics and unnecessary barriers that make it harder for eligible citizens to vote.
voting.quote: Erik will oppose voter suppression tactics that make it harder for eligible citizens to cast a ballot and have that ballot counted.

tax.text: She backed making the 2017 tax cuts permanent and said she carried a zero-based budgeting bill in the Minnesota Senate.
tax.quote: With Zero Based Budgeting, the budget would start from ZERO rather than the current approach of adjusting up or down from existing spending levels.

wages.text: She voted against the PRO Act, while saying she supports employees’ right to collectively bargain.
wages.quote: I voted against the PRO Act, which is a monumental rewrite of federal labor law that massively tips the scales in favor of Big Labor.

housing.text: She supported housing legislation aimed at streamlining permitting to speed homebuilding and increase affordable single-family homes.
housing.quote: Both initiatives focus on cutting through red tape and streamlining permitting to pave the way for faster homebuilding and increased availability of affordable, single-family homes in rural communities.

schools.text: She answered that she strongly supports school choice, including vouchers, tax credits, charter schools, private schools, and home schools.
schools.quote: I support school choice, including voucher programs, tax credits, charter schools, private schools, and home schools.

safety.text: She introduced legislation to provide education grants to students who commit to serving as law enforcement officers.
safety.quote: I am proud to introduce the Law Enforcement Education Grant Program Act to inspire the next generation and establish a targeted approach to specifically invest in well-trained and highly educated police officers.

immigration.text: She called for law enforcement to enforce immigration laws and opposed efforts to abolish ICE and promote sanctuary cities.
immigration.quote: we need to support law enforcement officials at all levels to enforce our immigration laws. I continue to stand up to efforts by the radical left to abolish Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and promote sanctuary cities.

guns.text: She said she would defend lawful gun owners’ right to keep and bear arms.
guns.quote: I will continue to defend the Constitutional right and vote to protect the right of every lawful gun owner in the United States to keep America free.

abortion.text: She said she supports legislation protecting life from conception and opposes federal funding for abortion.
abortion.quote: I will always support legislation that protects human life at all stages.

gender.toward: rules based on sex at birth
gender.text: She voted for legislation defining sex for school athletics by reproductive biology and genetics at birth.
gender.quote: This law states that sex in the athletic context must be recognized based only on a person's reproductive biology and genetics at birth.

cannabis.text: She voted against the MORE Act, which would have decriminalized cannabis federally and established a regulated tax structure for its sale.
cannabis.quote: the bill decriminalizes cannabis on the federal level, provides a taxation structure for the sale of cannabis

health.text: She criticized the Affordable Care Act and called for reforms that increase competition and offer families more health plan choices.
health.quote: I have and will continue to work to protect the promises we have made to our seniors and pass patient-centered reforms that increase competition and lower costs

energy.text: She introduced a bill aimed at halting policies she said raised gas prices and constrained domestic energy production.
energy.quote: I am proud to introduce this bill, which would stop these targeted policies from continuing until Americans start seeing gas cost $2.60 per gallon

voting.text: She joined a letter urging Minnesota to consider voter identification, ending same-day registration, and prohibiting automatic mailed ballots.
voting.quote: in future elections we urge you to consider best practices, such as voter identification, elimination of same-day voter registration, and prohibition of automatic mailed ballots.
